title: No Vibes Allowed: Solving Hard Problems in Complex Codebases – Dex Horthy, HumanLayer
talk_summary: Dex Horthy argues that coding-agent quality is dominated by context-window management: keep the agent in the 'smart zone' (roughly under 40% of the window) via research→plan→implement phases, intentional compaction into markdown artifacts, and sub-agents used purely to control context rather than to role-play. He also reframes code review as 'mental alignment' and insists humans must read plans/research because a bad plan line can cause a hundred bad code lines.

takeaways.what_they_do: Split work into a research phase (find the exact files/lines that matter, output a compact research doc), a planning phase (explicit steps with file names and code snippets plus how to test after each change), then implementation that just executes the plan, keeping each phase's context small.
takeaways.numbers: 2-3x more throughput claimed; 35,000 lines shipped in 7 hours on a 300k-line Rust codebase

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat ~40% of the context window as the point of diminishing returns; if a run is deep in the window, restart from a compacted summary rather than continuing to steer a degraded conversation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Around the 40% line is where you're going to start to see some diminishing returns
takeaways.numbers: ~40% of ~168k tokens as the soft ceiling

takeaways.technique: Sub-agents as context isolation, not personas
Review plans, not just diffs (mental alignment)
takeaways.what_they_do: Put the research/plan/agent thread on the PR so reviewers can follow intent and steps, and have humans review plans before implementation because a bad plan line is far more expensive than a bad code line.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a bad part of a plan is could be a hundred bad lines of code

takeaways.technique: Right-size the process to task difficulty
takeaways.what_they_do: Skip research/plan for trivial changes; use one research pass then a plan for medium multi-repo work; reserve full RPI for the hardest problems. Don't over-produce markdown for its own sake.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you're changing the color of a button, just talk to the agent and tell it what to do.

takeaways.technique: On-demand compressed context instead of stale repo docs
takeaways.what_they_do: Prefer generating a fresh research snapshot of the relevant slice of the codebase per task over maintaining long onboarding docs, because docs drift and become 'lies'.
takeaways.evidence_quote: What we prefer is on demand compressed context... We are compressing truth.
